## Goal
Remove the now-unused `'onImpact'` AOE projectile-detonation machinery (dead code retained by AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9) and its tests, now that no catalogue weapon uses the `'onImpact'` trigger.

## Context
AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9 moved the Mortar from `'onImpact'` to `'onRandom'`, so the `'onImpact'` path is no longer referenced by any weapon definition. Per project dead-code discipline it was deliberately retained during that change; this item is the follow-up cleanup (discovered-from:AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9).

## Scope (in)
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`: drop `'onImpact'` from the `AoETrigger` union; remove the `onImpact` descriptor doc; remove `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` if it has no remaining consumer (the Mortar's range basis is to be made explicit separately if needed).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts`: remove the `onAoeProjectileSpawned` hook and the `'onImpact'` branch in `_autoFire` (bullet spawn is then only unreachable; decide whether projectile spawn remains for any weapon).
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`, `detonateAoeProjectile`, the `bullet.aoeWeapon` handling in `onPlayerBulletHitsEnemy`, and the mortar VFX/sound path from `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` if unused.
- `src/entities/PlayerBullet.ts`: remove `aoeWeapon`, `aoeDetonated`, `onExpire` (if only used by the AOE path) and their comments.
- `src/scenes/core/AoeWeapons.test.ts`: remove the retained `onImpact` tests (the section marked 'Retained onImpact projectile-detonation machinery (dead code)').
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`: remove `onAoeProjectileSpawned`/`detonateAoeProjectile` from `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md`: update the descriptor union text (remove `'onImpact'`) and any remaining onImpact references.

## Out of scope
- Any behavioural change to Nova, Mortar or Arc.
- Removing the generic player-bullet spawn path used by conventional weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] AC1 — `AoETrigger` is `'onFire' | 'onRandom'`; no source references `'onImpact'` remain (except historical docs/changelog if intentionally kept — enumerate any).
- [ ] AC2 — The onImpact hooks/methods and `PlayerBullet` AOE fields are removed, and `npx tsc --noEmit` is clean.
- [ ] AC3 — The retained-onImpact tests are removed; `AoeWeapons.test.ts` still covers Nova/Arc/Mortar random detonation.
- [ ] AC4 — Gym↔game parity guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) still passes with the reduced `SHARED_AOE_METHODS`.
- [ ] AC5 — Docs (`docs/Game Design Document.md`) still pass `src/aoeDocs.test.ts` (or are updated if the guard references removed strings).
- [ ] AC6 — Full suite green (`/skill:test`).

## Notes / risks
- `spawnAoeDetonationVfx` (Mortar burst + cue, off-screen culling) is still needed by the `'onRandom'` path — do not remove it.
- The generic `spawnPlayerBullet` path must remain for the cannon/spread/dual/rapid.
- If any consumer of `AOE_PROJECTILE_SPEEDS` remains as the Mortar range basis, either keep it (renamed/documented) or replace the range basis explicitly; do not silently drop the Mortar range.

### Related work items
- **AH-0MUQUSFXB007NSLN** – F3: Mortar weapon — onImpact detonation (completed)
- **AH-0MUUF9GZV004WVT9** – Mortar detonates at a random point within weapon range (no forward projectile) (completed)
- **AH-0MV822C250051OVN** – Mortar projectile visuals & feel (completed)

- `README.md` — matched: ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac5 (+119 more)

# Halve bulletSpeed in unknown-archetype fallbacks

## Headline

Halve the `bulletSpeed` fallback from 200 to 100 in three unknown-archetype
fallbacks (`configStore.ts`, `difficultySequencer.ts`, `enemyDifficulty.ts`) so
that previously-out-of-scope edge cases fire at the same speed as the shipped
archetypes halved in AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ.

## Problem statement

AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ halved the `bulletSpeed` of all eight shipped archetypes
from 200 to 100 across the CSV, `DEFAULT_ENEMY_CONFIGS` and the per-entity
constants. Three additional runtime fallbacks for **unknown** archetype keys
were explicitly out of that item's scope:

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — `groupEnemyConfig()`

Leaving them at 200 means an unknown-key enemy fires at double the speed of
every shipped archetype.

## Users

- **Designers / tuners** — want consistent enemy behaviour regardless of
  archetype origin; an unknown-key enemy must not fire at double speed.
- **Producers / QA** — need predictable, balanced difficulty across all enemy
  configurations.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. AC1 — The three unknown-archetype fallbacks use `bulletSpeed: 100`
   (or a documented decision is recorded to leave them at 200 with rationale).
2. AC2 — Any difficulty-sequencer or difficulty-scoring test affected by the
   change is updated and the full test suite passes.
3. AC3 — The decision and rationale are recorded on this work item.

## Constraints

- The shipped archetype configurations are **not** changed (already handled in
  AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ).
- The change is purely numeric; no new logic or API surface is added.

## Existing state

Each of the three files contains a hard-coded `bulletSpeed: 200` in its
unknown-archetype fallback path.

## Desired change

Replace `bulletSpeed: 200` with `bulletSpeed: 100` in all three fallback
paths. Update any tests that assert on the previous value.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/configStore.ts` — line ~417, `genericEnemyDefault()`
- `src/core/difficultySequencer.ts` — line ~342, `resolveBaseConfig()`
- `src/core/enemyDifficulty.ts` — line ~316, `groupEnemyConfig()`

## Related work

- **AH-0MUWZ5GST003NMFQ** — Reduce bullet speed of enemies (parent discovery;
  shipped archetypes only, three fallbacks out of scope).
- **AH-0MUX60S9L0006NJ0** — Re-calibrate L4-L5 generated campaign targets after
  enemy bullet-speed halving (completed, non-blocking).

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Tests in `difficultySequencer` or `enemyDifficulty` may assert on
  `bulletSpeed: 200` for unknown-archetype paths — these must be updated.
  **Mitigation:** build + test before committing; check all test assertions.
- **Risk:** Gameplay balance shift for unknown-key enemies in edge cases.
  **Mitigation:** impact is minimal — these are rare edge cases with no shipped
  archetypes using them; the speed now matches the shipped baseline.
- **Scope:** This item touches only the three fallback paths listed above.
  Any new enemy archetype tuning is tracked as separate work.
- **Assumption:** The shipped archetype values (halved in the parent item) are
  the correct baseline; no further tuning is expected.

# Intake Brief — Make bot micro-simulation tests robust to small feel tweaks (AH-0MV03PVZI009870X)

## Problem statement

Several deterministic bot micro-simulation tests are knife-edge calibrations: a subtle, legitimate gameplay tweak (e.g. the 1–5% gentler thrust-press reduction in AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A) flips their outcomes because scores are dominated by discrete hit/bullet collisions. Each feel tweak requires manual seed recalibration, making tests brittle and opaque.

During AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A two tests had to be recalibrated:

- `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts` — the synthetic human seed moved 7 → 14. The base already regressed on 13/24 seeds; seed 14 is stable but this is a single-point fix.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` — `RUN_SEED` moved 0x0b07 → 0x0b16. On the new behaviour the competent bot wins on 20/32 seeds.

## Users

- **Gameplay engineers:** want test outcomes to reflect intentional design, not deterministic luck, so that bot-feel changes can be evaluated without hunting for lucky seeds.
- **Attract-mode observers:** want the demo-bot tests to demonstrate stable competence rather than a fragile calibration that could flip on any parameter change.

Example user stories:

- *As a gameplay engineer, I want the style-match demonstration to be stable across a range of seeds, so that I can tell whether a style-tuning change genuinely improved the fit rather than just shifting which seed wins.*
- *As a gameplay engineer, I want the competent-vs-legacy comparison to assert an objective-based advantage, so that the result reflects skill rather than chaotic bullet collisions.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The `evaluateStyleMatch` AC4 demonstration no longer depends on a single lucky seed: a test runs the styled-vs-structured comparison over a documented seed set (≥ 16 seeds) and asserts the styled bot is closer to human on a **majority** (≥ 50%) of those seeds with no competence regression on more than half. The existing seed-30 representative remains, but is no longer the sole determinant. Verified by a new multi-seed test that is re-run across the seed set and would fail if a single seed flipped.

- AC2: The competent-vs-legacy AC6 comparison asserts an **objective-based** advantage (minerals + power-ups + enemies priority score) rather than relying on the legacy bot's chaotic bullet collisions. This may be achieved by running on a bullet-free scenario and/or asserting on the objective sub-scores before collision penalties, over a documented seed set (≥ 16 seeds), with the competent bot winning on a **majority** (≥ 50%) of seeds. The current single-seed `RUN_SEED = 0x0b16` assertion is replaced or supplemented accordingly.

- AC3: Neither test requires re-seeding or recalibration when an unrelated small bot-feel tweak is applied. This is demonstrated by documenting the approach (e.g. a comment in each test explaining the aggregate/multi-seed rationale) and by ensuring the test asserts a distribution-stable property rather than a single cherry-picked outcome. A future tunable change to reaction time, thrust duration, or similar (that does not alter decision logic) does not cause either test to fail.

- AC4: The aggregate comparisons preserve full determinism — no `Math.random()` or non-seeded RNG; every seed is explicitly enumerated and reproducible.

- AC5: Full project test suite must pass with the new changes, including typecheck and build.

- AC6: All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **Determinism must be preserved.** Tests remain fully deterministic — no `Math.random()` or non-seeded RNG.
- **No behavioural change to bots.** Only the test harness / assertions change, not the bots themselves.
- **Aggregate, not cherry-pick.** Seeded comparisons must run over a documented range (≥ 16 seeds) and assert a majority-rule, not just pick the single seed where the desired outcome is strongest.
- **Surgical test changes.** Do not refactor the simulation harness or scoring infrastructure unless necessary — the goal is to make the existing tests robust, not to redesign them.
- **Test execution time.** Running 16+ seeds per test should remain cheap; the arena simulation is already headless (no Phaser, no wall clock).

## Existing state

### `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts`

- Uses `syntheticHumanRun(30, 420)` — a single carefully-chosen seed (30).
- The comment explains seed 30 was selected after the arena became config-driven (AH-0MV81YPBG0028WNM), but the base already regressed 13/24 seeds.
- The AC4 test (`it('demonstrates the styled bot is closer...')`) asserts `report.closer === true && report.regressed === false` on this single seed.

### `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts`

- Uses `RUN_SEED = 0x0b16` for the AC6 competent-vs-legacy comparison.
- The `REPRESENTATIVE` scenario includes 2 bullets (`{ x: 480, y: 20, vx: 0, vy: 60 }` and `{ x: 480, y: 520, vx: 0, vy: -60 }`).
- The `scoreOf()` function scores: minerals×4 + powerUps×3 + enemies×2 − asteroids×1 − collisions×5 − ticksSurvived×0.01. The collision penalty means chaotic bullet collisions can distort the score.
- A representative without bullets showed the legacy bot scoring higher (22 vs 20) on base, confirming bullets are the chaotic factor.

## Desired change

1. **Style-match (`evaluation.test.ts`):** Add a multi-seed test (e.g. `it('is stable across a seed sweep')`) that runs `evaluateStyleMatch` over ≥ 16 seeds (e.g. 0–15 or an explicit list) and asserts the styled bot is closer with no regression on the majority. Keep the existing single-seed test for readability but rename/document it as the representative case.

2. **Competent-vs-legacy (`competentBot.integration.test.ts`):** Add a multi-seed comparison (≥ 16 seeds) that asserts the competent bot wins on objective sub-scores (minerals/powerUps/enemies) over the majority. Either remove bullets from the comparison scenario or explicitly assert on `scoreOf()` with the collision term excluded/annotated. Keep `RUN_SEED = 0x0b16` as a documented representative seed.

3. **Document the rule:** Add a short comment in both tests explaining why aggregate/multi-seed assertions are used (to survive small feel tweaks) and how to add seeds.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/ai/style/evaluation.test.ts` — add multi-seed stability test; document the seed sweep rationale.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.integration.test.ts` — add multi-seed objective-advantage test; choose bullet-free or sub-score assertion.
- `src/ai/eval/arena.ts` — arena runner; may need no change but is the simulation entry point.
- `src/ai/style/evaluation.ts` — `evaluateStyleMatch`; may need no change but is the function under test.
- `docs/` — any docs describing the bot A/B or evaluation harness (check `docs/Game Design Document.md` demo-bot subsection and any eval docs) need a line about aggregate seed-based assertions.

## Related work

- **AH-0MUYRJQE50021T4A — Bot is more gentle on the thrusters** (completed) — introduced the 1–5% thrust-press reduction that caused the two test recalibrations. This item is the follow-up to fix the root cause (brittle tests).
- **AH-0MUY08WX3000ZEVO — Structured competent bot: utility goals, behaviour tree, predictive dodge/aim** (completed) — the competent bot whose AC6 test we are hardening.
- **AH-0MUY08XXN003NV0I — Style match evaluation** (completed) — introduced the `evaluateStyleMatch` / AC4 test.
- **AH-0MUY08V6W001SJJN — Deterministic run seeding and seed plumbing** (completed) — the run-seeding infrastructure that enables multi-seed testing.
- **AH-0MUY08XLD009K4W4 — Same-seed evaluation harness: metrics, A/B, side-by-side** (completed) — the evaluation report infrastructure.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "Robust" means majority-rule over ≥ 16 seeds, not full distributional analysis. If the producer wants statistical significance (e.g. 95% CI, p-value), that would increase scope; record as a separate item.
- **Risk — aggregate threshold selection (scope/validity):** choosing "majority" (≥ 50%) is simple but may be too lenient. The implementer should pick a threshold (≥ 50%, ideally ≥ 67%) and document why; a too-generous threshold weakens the test.
- **Risk — test execution time:** running 16+ seeds per test could increase test time. The arena simulation is already headless (no Phaser, no wall clock), so the cost should be modest; measure before committing.
- **Risk — scope creep:** it is tempting to also fix other knife-edge micro-simulations (or redesign the scoring). Those are out of scope; file separate items if discovered.
- **Failure mode:** if the multi-seed test only cherry-picks seeds that pass, it recreates the original problem. The seed set must be documented and contiguous (or explicitly listed), and the assertion must be majority-based.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: *How many seeds should the aggregate tests run over?* — Answer (from work-item description, inferred): ≥ 16 seeds, asserting majority-rule. This balances robustness with test speed. Source: AC1/AC2 wording ("multiple seeds", "not a single lucky seed").
- Q: *Should the AC6 comparison remove bullets from the scenario, or assert on sub-scores?* — Answer (documented assumption): either approach is acceptable. The brief notes both options; the implementer should choose the cleaner approach. The key is objective-based advantage, not collision-inflated score. Source: AC2 ("asserts an objective-based advantage rather than relying on chaotic bullet collisions").

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MU732AJW005RTG1** – Write tests for new game scenes and systems (completed)
- **AH-0MUUM3KYX008ABSW** – Test migration + verify: Update existing tests and verify parity (completed)
- **AH-0MV03GXZQ00801T4** – Bot prioritises extra lives in hold-full choice and on-screen pickups (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: 0muyrjqe50021t4a, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, ac6, already, assert, asserts, base, based, behaviour, bot, build, bullet, bullets, chaotic, collisions, compare, competent, competentbot, demonstration, depends, deterministic, discovered, discrete, edge, either, feel, framework, full, gameplay, gentler, had, higher, hit, human, integration, legacy, longer, make, match, micro, moved, multiple, objective, outcomes, over, pass, picked, press, rather, reduction, required, robust, run, score, scores, seed, seeds, set, several, simulation, single, small, src, style, styled, subtle, suite, test, tests, their, thrust, two, unrelated, whose, wins
- `README.md` — matched: 0muyrjqe50021t4a, ac1, ac2, ac3, ac4, acceptance, advantage, aggregate, already, assert, asserts, base, based, behaviour, bot, build, bullet, bullets, collisions, compare, competence, criteria, depends, deterministic, discovered, dominated, edge, either, evaluation, feel, framework, full, gameplay, goal, had, higher, hit, human, integration, legacy, longer, make, match, moved, multiple, outcomes, over, pass, picked, press, problem, rather, required, robust, run, scenarios, score, seed, seeds, set, several, simulation, single, small, src, style, styled, suite, synthetic, test, tests, their, thrust, two, unrelated, whose

# Navigation of Gym menu (AH-0MV1BKZ0J00946EX)

## Problem statement

The dev-mode Gym Index (`GymIndex`) lays its launch rows out in three columns
(plain scenes | ENEMIES | Dev Utilities), but keyboard focus moves through
every row as a single linear, wrapping list. The arrow keys therefore do not
match the on-screen spatial layout: Right from the bottom of a column jumps to
the next column's first row, and there is no deliberate way to step
left/right between columns. A keyboard-only developer cannot navigate the
index the way they read it.

## Users

Developers/testers who exercise the gym scenes, and keyboard-only or
accessibility users who expect the in-canvas UI to match its visual layout.

**User stories**

- As a keyboard-only developer, I want **Left/Right** to move focus between the
  three columns, so that I can reach the column I want without tabbing through
  every row.
- As a keyboard-only developer, I want **Up/Down** to move focus within the
  current column, so that I can choose a row in that column predictably.
- As a keyboard-only developer, I want the focused row to stay highlighted and
  **Enter/Space** to launch it exactly as before, so that the new navigation
  does not break activation.
- As a maintainer, I want the grid behaviour to be **opt-in** in the shared
  focus manager, so that every other menu keeps its current linear Tab/arrow
  behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Opt-in grid navigation; existing behaviour unchanged.** The shared
  `FocusManager` (or a small shared helper alongside it) gains an opt-in
  column-aware navigation mode. Scenes that do not opt in keep today's linear
  Tab / Shift+Tab / arrow cycling with wrap-around. *Verification:* the
  existing `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` passes unchanged, and a new test
  asserts the default mode is still linear.
- **AC2 — Left/Right move between Gym Index columns.** With grid navigation
  enabled, **Right** moves focus to the adjacent column on the right and
  **Left** to the adjacent column on the left, wrapping from the rightmost
  column to the leftmost and vice versa. Focus never lands on a non-row
  (title, headers or hint). *Verification:* a unit test in
  `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` asserts the focused column changes on
  ArrowLeft/ArrowRight and wraps at both ends.
- **AC3 — Up/Down move within the current column.** **Down** moves focus to
  the next row in the current column and **Up** to the previous row, wrapping
  within the column (top ↔ bottom). Up/Down never change column.
  *Verification:* a unit test asserts vertical movement and per-column
  wrap-around without leaving the column.
- **AC4 — Uneven columns always land on a valid row.** The columns have
  different row counts (plain scenes: many; ENEMIES: 3; Dev Utilities: 1).
  Moving horizontally into a shorter column focuses a valid, highlighted row
  (clamping rule documented below) — never an out-of-range index or a
  non-row. *Verification:* a unit test drives focus to the bottom of the
  longest column, presses Right into the shortest column, and asserts a real
  row is focused and highlighted.
- **AC5 — Activation, pointer and ESC unchanged.** Enter/Space still activate
  the focused row through the same callback as a pointer click (plain scene,
  Fodder Enemies, Boss, Mini-Boss, Dev Utilities), pointer clicks still work
  for every row, ESC still returns to the main menu, and SHUTDOWN still
  detaches the keyboard listener and clears the focus registry.
  *Verification:* the existing GymIndex activation/pointer/ESC/shutdown tests
  remain green, plus a new test activating a row after moving between columns.
- **AC6 — Hint and documentation updated.** `GYM_INDEX_HINT` and every doc that
  enumerates keyboard navigation describe Left/Right column movement and
  Up/Down row movement. *Verification:* inspection of the hint and the updated
  docs sections.
- **AC7 — Tests, docs and full suite.** New/updated tests cover AC1–AC5. All
  related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries. The full
  project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Scope is the **Gym Index screen** (`GymIndex`), **not** the internal menus of
  individual gym scenes and **not** the other menu-style scenes.
- Reuse the shared `FocusManager`; do **not** add a second ad-hoc focus/key
  handler inside `GymIndex`.
- The default (non-grid) behaviour must remain the current linear behaviour
  for every other consumer (`MenuScene`, `GameOverScene`, `PauseScene`,
  `HelpScene`, `LeaderboardScene`, `TelemetryConsentScene`, and the Hangar War
  screens).
- Pointer handlers, ESC-to-menu, row ordering and the column layout (X
  positions) must not change.
- No CI/CD pipeline tests (per intake convention). `CHANGELOG.md` is excluded
  (managed by the ship skill).
- No new npm dependencies.

## Existing state

- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` renders three columns and registers every row with
  the shared `FocusManager` in reading order (plain scenes → ENEMIES → Dev
  Utilities). `GYM_INDEX_HINT` currently reads
  `tab/arrows move · enter/space select · ESC returns to menu`.
- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` maps Tab / Shift+Tab and **every** arrow key
  onto linear `cycleFocus(±1)` with wrap-around; it has no notion of columns or
  axis. It is used by `MenuScene`, `GameOverScene`, `PauseScene`, `HelpScene`,
  `LeaderboardScene`, `TelemetryConsentScene` and the Hangar War screens.
- `GymIndex` exposes test accessors `listedScenes`, `listedEnemyScenes`,
  `listedDevUtilityScenes`, `getFocusedIndex`, `getFocusedLabel` and
  `getFocusControlCount`. Column X positions are exported as
  `GYM_INDEX_COLUMN_X`.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` already has a keyboard-navigation block that
  asserts the current linear order and wrap; those arrow assertions will need
  updating to the new semantics (Tab/activation/ESC coverage is kept).
- 2-D/grid navigation was explicitly deferred in AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE (linear
  cycling shipped instead); this item is the follow-up that delivers it.

## Desired change

1. Extend the shared `FocusManager` with an **opt-in** column-aware mode (for
   example `attachKeyboard(scene, { navigation: 'grid', columns: [...] })` or an
   `attachGridKeyboard(scene, columns)` helper). Columns are ordered lists of
   controls (or focus indices) in visual order; the default path stays exactly
   as today.
2. In `GymIndex.create()`, register the existing three columns with grid mode,
   using the same `registerRow` activation callbacks.
3. Implement the horizontal/vertical movement rules (including wrap and
   shorter-column clamping) and keep Enter/Space activation unchanged.
4. Update `GYM_INDEX_HINT`, the module doc comment and the README
   keyboard-navigation / Gym Index sections.
5. Update/extend `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` and
   `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` to cover grid mode while keeping linear mode
   covered.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/utils/focusManager.ts` — add opt-in grid/column navigation while
  preserving the current linear default.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.ts` — opt into grid navigation, pass the three columns,
  update the hint and module doc comment.
- `src/utils/focusManager.test.ts` — cover grid-mode movement and confirm the
  linear default is untouched.
- `src/scenes/GymIndex.test.ts` — cover Left/Right column movement (with wrap),
  Up/Down within-column movement, uneven-column clamping, activation after a
  column move, and the updated hint.
- `README.md` — update the keyboard-only navigation section and the Gym Index
  section (~lines 391 and ~417) to describe column/row arrows.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — §8.5 keyboard-operability note if
  it enumerates Gym Index navigation.

## Related work

- AH-0MUDZFBYY008P7ZE — Gym scenes index not navigable by keyboard (delivered
  linear `FocusManager` navigation; explicitly deferred 2-D/grid navigation).
  *Completed.*
- AH-0MUBZT64O0056BRY — Reusable in-canvas focus manager (the shared utility
  to extend). *Completed.*
- AH-0MV13G5EV008D41E — Single enemy gym scene with in-panel selector;
  established the current three-column index layout. *Completed.*
- AH-0MUGXDVPH005TIZL — Dev Utilities gym scene / column. *Completed.*
- AH-0MU9LKQEP008LCX9 — Keyboard only control (umbrella). *Completed.*

## Risks & assumptions

**Risks**

- **FocusManager regression.** The utility is used by eight scenes; a careless
  change could alter their arrow-key behaviour. Mitigation: opt-in mode only,
  default unchanged, plus the existing FocusManager tests and the full-suite
  gate.
- **Test churn.** The existing GymIndex keyboard tests assert linear arrow
  order; they must be updated to the new arrow semantics while keeping
  Tab/activation/ESC coverage. Mitigation: keep Tab's behaviour explicit and
  test both models.
- **Uneven-column UX.** A naive clamp can make focus jump unexpectedly when
  moving to a shorter column and back. Mitigation: document the rule and test
  it; sticky per-column row memory is a small, contained follow-up if wanted.
- **Scope creep.** Grid navigation for other scenes (Leaderboard grid, hex
  map) or mouse-free gym internals is out of scope; record as linked
  follow-ups rather than expanding this change.

**Assumptions (confirmed by producer, 2026-11-07)**

- Grid mode is **opt-in** and **GymIndex-only** in this change.
- Left/Right **wrap** between columns (rightmost → leftmost and vice versa),
  matching the existing wrap convention.
- Up/Down **wrap within the current column** (top → bottom and bottom → top)
  and never change column.
- On entering a shorter column, focus **clamps to the last valid row** of that
  column (no per-column row memory in this change).
- **Tab keeps its current linear cycling** through all rows in reading order;
  only the arrow keys become grid-aware.
- Activation (Enter/Space), pointer handling and ESC behaviour are unchanged.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

The producer answered all five questions with option **(a)** — the recommended
option — confirming the working assumptions recorded during the auto-dispatched
intake.

**Q1 — Should Left/Right wrap between columns, or clamp at the outer
columns?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Wrap** — rightmost column → leftmost, and vice
  versa. Confirms the working assumption. Source: interactive reply,
  2026-11-07.

**Q2 — Should Up/Down stay within the current column, or move across columns
at the top/bottom edge?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Stay within the column and wrap top ↔ bottom.**
  Confirms the working assumption. Source: interactive reply, 2026-11-07.

**Q3 — How should focus behave when moving into a shorter column (for example
Dev Utilities has a single row)?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Clamp to the last valid row of the target column;
  no per-column "remembered row".** Confirms the working assumption. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-07.

**Q4 — Should Tab remain linear cycling through all rows, or also become
grid-aware?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Keep Tab linear; only the arrow keys are
  grid-aware.** Confirms the working assumption. Source: interactive reply,
  2026-11-07.

**Q5 — Should grid navigation be a shared opt-in `FocusManager` mode, or local
to `GymIndex`?**

- Answer (producer): **(a) Shared opt-in `FocusManager` mode, with the default
  linear behaviour unchanged.** Confirms the working assumption. Source:
  interactive reply, 2026-11-07. Research: inspected
  `src/utils/focusManager.ts` (linear-only today) and its consumers; no
  existing grid mode.

# Wave Laser Audio Polish & Leveling Gym Round-Robin

## Problem Statement

The wave laser fires with audio (the fire cue already exists in `playWeaponFireSound`), but it has no dedicated pickup activation cue and is excluded from the weapon-leveling gym's round-robin drop cycle — unlike every other weapon except reset. Audio and gym parity with the rest of the weapon catalogue is incomplete.

## Users

- **Player (game)**: Hearing a distinct, satisfying pickup sound when collecting a wave laser drop, consistent with spread/dual/rapid/r reset pickups.
- **Player (leveling gym)**: Seeing the wave laser appear in the leveling gym's round-robin drop cycle so it can be tested and levelled like other weapons.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A `playWaveLaserPickupSound()` function exists in `src/audio/effects.ts`, calling `playCue('playWaveLaserPickupSound')`, following the pattern of `playSpreadPickupSound`/`playDualPickupSound`/`playRapidPickupSound`.
- The baked cue `playWaveLaserPickupSound` (recipe: `aihell-pickup-wave-laser`) is registered in `audio/toneforge/manifest.json`.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` imports `playWaveLaserPickupSound` and adds a `'wave_laser'` case to the `weaponDropId` switch in `playDropPickupCue`, dispatching it alongside the generic collect-pop sound.
- The wave laser pickup cue plays when the player collects a wave laser drop in both the game (`PlayScene`) and all gyms that exercise weapon pickups.
- **Leveling gym (optional / producer decision needed):** `'wave_laser'` is added to `LEVELING_DROP_ORDER` in `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts`, placed after `'arc'` (alphabetical grouping) or at a producer-specified position.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- Follow the existing ToneForge baked-cue pipeline (no procedural Web Audio); new audio must go through the `playCue()` manifest-dispatch path.
- The pickup cue should be distinct from and proportionally shorter than the existing spread/dual/rapid/reset pickup cues, so a refused pickup remains audibly distinct.
- The wave laser fire cue already exists in `playWeaponFireSound` — do not modify it.

## Existing State

- **Fire cue:** Already implemented. `src/audio/effects.ts` line ~1077 has the `wave_laser` case in `playWeaponFireSound`, applying `WAVE_LASER_VOLUME_SCALE`.
- **Impact cue:** Already implemented (`playWaveLaserImpactSound`).
- **Pickup cue:** Missing entirely — no `playWaveLaserPickupSound` function, no manifest entry.
- **Leveling gym:** `LEVELING_DROP_ORDER` contains spread, dual, rapid, nova, mortar, arc, rear_guard, broadside, railgun, shard_swarm, heavy_slug — excludes wave_laser (and ricochet, cluster, options).

## Desired Change

1. Add the wave laser pickup sound through the ToneForge baked-cue pipeline.
2. Wire the pickup cue into `dropLayer.ts`'s `playDropPickupCue` switch.
3. **(Producer decision)** Add `'wave_laser'` to `LEVELING_DROP_ORDER` in `GymWeaponLeveling.ts`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Add `playWaveLaserPickupSound()` export (after `playResetPickupSound`).
- `audio/toneforge/manifest.json` — Register `playWaveLaserPickupSound` / `aihell-pickup-wave-laser`.
- `src/scenes/core/dropLayer.ts` — Import and add `'wave_laser'` case to `playDropPickupCue`'s `weaponDropId` switch.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeaponLeveling.ts` — Add `'wave_laser'` to `LEVELING_DROP_ORDER` (if producer approves).
- `src/audio/effects.test.ts` — Add unit test for `playWaveLaserPickupSound` dispatch.
- `src/utils/weaponFeelRoster.test.ts` — Ensure wave_laser is included in the full roster coverage (fire is already covered; verify pickup coverage if the test checks all weapons).

## Related Work

- **AH-0MV1BIUSJ0090W92** — R-Type piercing wave laser (parent, completed/shipped). Created the wave laser as a playable weapon; noted audio cues and leveling-gym round-robin as a follow-up.
- **AH-0MV2K5SR0005RTTE** — Variety in weapon graphics (completed). Documented the audio pipeline and baked ToneForge cue requirements.
- **AH-0MW10J31B0053E56** — Wave Laser tuning (completed). Tuned fire/impact parameters.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Risk:** The ToneForge baked-cue pipeline requires a new audio asset (recipe + manifest entry). If the producer has not yet produced the wave laser pickup sound, implementation may need to wait or use a placeholder.
- **Assumption:** The wave laser pickup sound design has been approved as part of the wave laser's audio package. If not, this work item blocks on the audio asset.
- **Scope creep risk:** Adding ALL missing weapon pickup cues (ricochet, cluster, options, railgun, shard_swarm, rear_guard, broadside, heavy_slug, nova, mortar, arc) would significantly increase scope. Keep scope to wave_laser only; file separate items for other weapons if needed.
- **Assumption:** Adding wave_laser to `LEVELING_DROP_ORDER` is desirable. If the producer considers wave_laser too powerful or too niche for the gym, it can be deferred.

## Open Questions for Producer

1. **Leveling gym inclusion:** Should `'wave_laser'` be added to `LEVELING_DROP_ORDER` in `GymWeaponLeveling.ts`? It is currently the only catalogue weapon (besides ricochet, cluster, and options) excluded from the leveling gym's round-robin.
2. **Audio asset status:** Has the wave laser pickup sound been produced in ToneForge, or does it need to be created before this work can proceed?

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions & Answers

- Q: "Should wave_laser be added to LEVELING_DROP_ORDER?" — Answer: OPEN QUESTION — awaiting producer decision. The work item says "optionally include", implying discretion.
- Q: "Is the wave_laser fire cue really missing?" — Research: inspected `src/audio/effects.ts` `playWeaponFireSound` switch (line ~1077) — wave_laser case EXISTS with `WAVE_LASER_VOLUME_SCALE`. The original work-item description was written before this was implemented. Corrected: only the pickup cue is missing.

## Impact

Collecting a wave laser drop now plays its own short rising shimmer — distinct from every other weapon pickup — and the wave laser can be levelled in the weapon-leveling gym alongside the rest of the arsenal.

# Gym recharge-time tuning sliders (dedicated tuning gym)

## Problem statement

Phase Shift and Teleport now recharge per charge, but their recharge times are
level-derived only (`phaseRechargeRate` 30 s → 10 s, `teleportRechargeRate`
60 s → 20 s). A balance observer cannot answer "what if Teleport recharged in
8 s?" without editing the level catalogue and reloading. There is no place to
watch the two defensive abilities cycle under sustained threat while varying
their recharge times.

## Users

- **Balance tuner (primary):** needs a dedicated gym where Phase Shift and
  Teleport are permanently owned from the first frame and attacked from more
  than one direction, with live sliders for each recharge time — so recharge
  pacing can be judged by eye and the chosen value persisted for the next
  session.
- **Producer / designer (secondary):** needs the tuning knobs to stay
  gym-only, so shipped gameplay defaults are never changed by accident.

Example user stories:

- *As a balance tuner, I want a gym that starts me with Phase Shift and
  Teleport already owned, so I do not have to farm drops before observing a
  recharge cycle.*
- *As a balance tuner, I want two groups of shooting enemies so both
  defensive abilities are triggered repeatedly from different directions.*
- *As a balance tuner, I want to drag a "Phase Shift recharge" slider and see
  the next spent charge return in the new time, and have that value survive a
  page reload.*

## Acceptance Criteria

- A new dedicated gym scene `GymRechargeTuning` (`src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.ts`) spawns the player at screen centre with **Phase Shift and Teleport granted as permanent power-ups from the first frame** (each a recharging charge pool, cap 3), so both abilities auto-activate under threat without collecting a drop.
- The gym spawns **at least two groups of shooting `raider` enemies** (default 3 per group, placed left and right of the player) with shooting enabled by default, plus an in-panel SHOOT toggle and the shared wave-timeout refresh, so threat pressure is sustained.
- Two live sliders ("Phase Shift recharge" and "Teleport recharge") live in a plain-DOM `.gym-panel`, reuse the `buildSpawnIntervalSlider` pattern, cover **Phase 1–60 s / Teleport 1–120 s at 0.5 s steps**, display **seconds**, and **immediately change the recharge time applied to subsequently spent charges**.
- Slider values **persist via the rules config** as `phaseRechargeOverrideSeconds` / `teleportRechargeOverrideSeconds` (`number | null`; `null`/absent = level-derived default) and are re-applied on scene create; the gym seeds each slider from the persisted override or the level-derived default when unset.
- The override is **gym-only**: the shipped `PlayScene` and every other gym keep level-derived recharge times (the override is read by the tuning gym, not applied to gameplay defaults).
- Unit tests cover the slider DOM (ids, labels, min/max/step, output), live application to the recharge timers, the rules persistence round-trip, the `null` fallback, and the two-group enemy spawn with shooting on — in `src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.test.ts`.
- A `GymRechargeTuning` row is added to `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` recording its enabled objects, spawn seam and any retained divergence (guarded by `src/scenes/core/gymParityDocs.test.ts`).
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Gym ↔ game parity:** the new gym must consume the shared seams — `createEnemyFromConfig` + `resolveSpawnTransitTarget` for spawning, the shared wave timeout, `CombatScene`/`CombatCoreScene` helpers — not a divergent copy (AGENTS.md Game Architecture Conventions).
- **Reuse the slider pattern:** extend `src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts` with a recharge slider builder and persist helper rather than duplicating the DOM code.
- **Do not change shipped defaults:** the level catalogue's recharge rates stay authoritative for gameplay; the override is an optional gym/rules layer.
- **Backward-compatible rules blob:** new optional fields coerce to `null` when absent; existing saved rules must still load.
- **Run-scoped timers:** the override applies to timer durations set at consumption; in-flight timers are not retro-fitted (matching the run-scoped recharge model).
- **Auto-discovery:** `GymIndex` discovers `Gym*.ts` automatically, so no index registration edit is needed — but the parity row is still mandatory.

## Existing state

- **Recharge model:** `PowerUpLevelStore` (`src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts`) tracks per-charge recharge timers; `phaseRechargeTime()` / `teleportRechargeTime()` derive seconds from the level axes (`phaseRechargeRate` 1/30 → 1/10 charges/s; `teleportRechargeRate` 1/60 → 1/20 charges/s); `EffectsRegistry.tick` advances `tickRecharge(dt)`.
- **No override mechanism:** recharge time is level-derived only; there is no rules-level or store-level override.
- **Slider precedent:** `src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts` exports `buildSpawnIntervalSlider(onApply)` and `applyAndPersistSpawnInterval(seconds)`; used by `GymBoss` and `GymFodderEnemies`.
- **Permanent grants:** `grantPermanentPowerUp(id, effectsRegistry)` → `effectsRegistry.applyCollect(id, true)` (`src/powerups/choiceReward.ts`).
- **Reference scene shape:** `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` (player + 3-scout V-formation, SHOOT toggle, wave timeout, shared `CombatScene`).

## Desired change

- Add an optional recharge-time override seam to `PowerUpLevelStore` (e.g. `setRechargeTimeOverride(phaseSeconds | null, teleportSeconds | null)`) honoured by `phaseRechargeTime()` / `teleportRechargeTime()`, falling back to the level-derived value when unset.
- Add optional `phaseRechargeOverrideSeconds` / `teleportRechargeOverrideSeconds` (`number | null`) to `GameRules`, its defaults and `loadRules` coercion.
- Add `buildRechargeTimeSlider(...)` and a persist helper to `src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts`.
- Create the `GymRechargeTuning` scene: player + permanent Phase Shift/Teleport grants, two `raider` groups with SHOOT on, panel with the two recharge sliders wired to the store override and rules persistence.
- Add tests, the parity row and the documentation note.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.ts` — New scene: player, permanent grants, two raider groups, tuning panel.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymRechargeTuning.test.ts` — Slider DOM, live application, persistence, fallback and spawn tests.
- `src/utils/gymPowerUpControl.ts` — Add a recharge-time slider builder + persist helper.
- `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` — Recharge-time override seam on `PowerUpLevelStore`.
- `src/core/rules.ts` — Optional override fields, defaults and load coercion.
- `src/core/rules.test.ts` — Persistence/coercion tests for the new fields.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — Add the `GymRechargeTuning` parity row.
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — Note the gym-only tuning control if the levelling section describes recharge.

## Related work

- AH-0MV2N0FX2004KEPR — Teleport and Phase Shift should recharge (parent/recharge model).
- AH-0MW231MCL000MMUU — Store readiness: spending Teleport starts the timer.
- AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4 — Teleport regenerates too quickly.
- AH-0MV82IA9U004BOKP — HUD recharge countdown indicator (sibling follow-up).
- AH-0MV82IAM7004KOYQ — Recharge-complete audio cue (sibling follow-up).
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 — Gym ↔ game parity convention.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What is being tuned — which abilities and which property?" — Answer (producer): "Phase Shift and Teleport recharge times." Source: interactive reply (intake round 1).
- Q: "Which gym scene(s) should get the recharge sliders?" — Answer (producer): "Create a Gym specifically for tuning these. It should spawn a player who has them as permanent power-ups from the start. There should be at least two groups of shooting enemies." Final: a new dedicated `GymRechargeTuning` scene. Source: interactive reply (intake round 2).
- Q: "How should the sliders override recharge — absolute time, a multiplier, or both?" — Answer (producer): "1. A". Final: (A) absolute recharge time in seconds, applied as an override on the level-derived value. Source: interactive reply (intake round 3).
- Q: "What should the two enemy groups be?" — Answer (producer): "2. B you choose". Final: two groups of `raider` archetype (3 per group, left and right), chosen for mobile aimed fire that creates converging, sustained pressure; `EnemyConfig` remains the retuning surface. Source: interactive reply (intake round 3).
- Q: "Slider count, range, display and persistence?" — Answer: implied acceptance of the stated defaults (two sliders; Phase 1–60 s / Teleport 1–120 s at 0.5 s steps; display seconds; persist via rules with `null` = level-derived), since the producer answered only the two explicit questions and did not object to the defaults. Source: interactive reply (intake round 3); recorded as an assumption for producer confirmation at plan/review.


## Impact

A balance tuner can open a dedicated gym where Phase Shift and Teleport are already owned and under sustained raider fire, drag a slider to change either recharge time and watch the next spent charge come back in the new time, with the chosen value surviving a page reload while shipped gameplay keeps its level-derived defaults.

## Implementation notes & assumptions

- **Teleport `cap 3` wording.** The work item's AC parenthetical says both abilities are "a recharging charge pool, cap 3". Phase Shift is a pooled consumable whose regenerating ceiling is 3 and is honoured exactly. Teleport is **single-use** in the shipped recharge model (parent AH-0MVY096RT006QMF4): its whole state is one readiness timer (cap 1). Giving it a stored multi-charge pool would change shipped gameplay, which this gym must not do, so the gym grants Teleport permanently (leaving its single warp ready) and exposes its level-derived recharge time through the same slider/override seam. Recorded as a reasonable assumption for producer confirmation at review.
- **Gym-only override.** `PowerUpLevelStore.setRechargeTimeOverride(phaseSeconds, teleportSeconds)` is read only by the tuning gym; `GameRules.phaseRechargeOverrideSeconds` / `teleportRechargeOverrideSeconds` default to `null` (level-derived) and coerce absent/corrupt values to `null`, so existing rules blobs are backward-compatible. `PlayScene` and every other gym never read the override.
- **Run-scoped timers.** The override is resolved when a charge is spent, so it applies to subsequently spent charges; an in-flight timer keeps the duration captured at spend time (covered by tests).
- **Auto-discovery + registries.** The scene is discovered automatically by `GymIndex`; the capture registry (`scripts/capture-scenes.mjs`), `examples/scenes.json`, `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, the parity guard's scene list and the GymIndex ordering test were updated to match.
- **Test evidence.** Full suite green at the implementation commit: 10,549 tests passed (467 files). Changed-scope gate covers `GymRechargeTuning.test.ts`, `rules.test.ts`, `powerUpLevels.test.ts`, `gymParityDocs.test.ts` and `capture-scenes.test.ts`.

# Objective

Give asteroid entities the **lowest render depth** ("furthest away" z value) of
any foreground gameplay object, so a drifting rock always draws behind the
player ship, every other enemy, bullets, minerals and power-ups — while still
drawing above the background and juice layers. One named constant, applied once
on the shared `Asteroid` entity, so the game and every asteroid-bearing gym stay
in parity by construction.

## Problem statement

Asteroids are inert, drifting **world hazards** that should read as distant
scenery, but they currently render at the default gameplay depth (`0`) — the
same depth as the player, every enemy, minerals and power-ups — so their visual
order is decided purely by scene display-list insertion order. Because the
scheduled spawner releases asteroids *during* a wave (after the formation
enemies are added) their containers are appended last and therefore draw **on
top of** ships and other enemies. A large rock can visibly occlude a scout or
the player, which reads as the rock being in front of the action rather than
behind it.

## Users / user stories

- **As a player**, when an asteroid drifts across a formation of enemies, I want
  it to pass *behind* them so the action stays legible and the rock reads as
  distant scenery, not a foreground object.
- **As a player**, I want bullets, minerals and power-ups to stay clearly
  visible above asteroids so pickups and shots are never hidden by a rock.
- **As a developer / gym author**, I want the asteroid depth defined once on the
  shared entity so the game and every gym render it identically with no
  per-scene wiring.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Asteroid entities render at the **lowest foreground depth**: strictly below
  every other gameplay object (player, all other enemy archetypes, bullets,
  minerals, power-ups) and strictly above every background layer
  (`BACKGROUND_DEPTH`, `BACKGROUND_DIM_DEPTH`, `BACKGROUND_WARP_DEPTH`).
- The depth is a **single named constant** (e.g. `ASTEROID_DEPTH`) exported
  from `src/core/constants.ts` and applied **once** in the `Asteroid`
  constructor, so all spawn paths — the scheduled spawner
  (`createAsteroidFromEvent`), `PlayScene.spawnAsteroidAt`, the shared
  `splitAsteroid` children, and every gym spawn — inherit the same value with no
  per-call wiring.
- A focused unit test asserts that a newly constructed `Asteroid` **and** a
  split child both expose `depth === ASTEROID_DEPTH`, that the value is
  strictly less than the gameplay baseline (`0`) and strictly greater than the
  background layers, and that the existing **intra-entity** layer order
  (body/force-field/explosion) is unchanged.
- Gym↔game parity: an asteroid spawned through the shared seam in the game and
  in an asteroid-bearing gym resolve the identical depth (pinned by a test and
  the parity docs), so no scene can diverge.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the change — code comments,
  `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` (E6 asteroid section and/or render
  layering note), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` where relevant, and the GDD if it
  documents render layering — and the full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- The change must live on the **shared `Asteroid` entity** (and a shared
  constant), never on a per-scene spawn path, to satisfy the gym↔game parity
  convention in `AGENTS.md` § Game Architecture Conventions.
- The asteroid must stay **above** the background photo, its dim overlay and the
  hyperspace-warp layers; "lowest" means lowest **foreground** layer, not below
  the backdrop.
- Do **not** change the asteroid's intra-container child depths (body `1`,
  force-field `1.5`, explosion `2`) or their relative order — only the
  container's own scene depth.
- No gameplay behaviour change: motion, wrapping, splitting, collision, scoring
  and audio are untouched. This is a **render-order-only** change.
- Must not affect non-asteroid enemies, the boss, bullets or pickups.

## Existing state

- **Phaser render ordering.** In Phaser (v4.2.1) a `GameObject`'s `depth`
  property is the "z-index" used for display-list render order; higher depth
  renders on top. `setDepth()` is the mechanism.
- **Depth layers already defined** in `src/core/constants.ts`:
  `BACKGROUND_DEPTH = -1000`, `BACKGROUND_DIM_DEPTH = -950`,
  `BACKGROUND_WARP_DEPTH = -900`, `HUD_DEPTH = 1000`; and in
  `src/core/constants.ts` / entity modules: `MINERAL_DEPTH = 2`,
  `MYSTERY_UFO_DRONE_DEPTH = 2`, bullets at `3`.
- **Every enemy (including `Asteroid`) extends `BaseEnemy`, a
  `Phaser.GameObjects.Container`,** and none of them set the container's own
  depth, so they all render at the default gameplay depth `0`. Their internal
  child graphics set depths **within** the container (`src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts`:
  body `1`, force-field `1.5`, explosion `2`).
- **All asteroid spawn paths construct the `Asteroid` entity directly**:
  `src/scenes/core/asteroidHazard.ts::createAsteroidFromEvent`,
  `PlayScene.spawnAsteroidAt`, and `src/scenes/core/asteroidSplit.ts`
  (`splitAsteroid` children). Gym spawns go through the same entity/factory. A
  depth set in the entity constructor therefore covers every path.
- There is **no existing z/depth column** in `src/data/enemy-configs.csv` and no
  documented asteroid render-order convention in the design docs — this item
  establishes that convention.

## Desired change

1. Add a named `ASTEROID_DEPTH` constant in `src/core/constants.ts` (value `-1`
   unless the implementer has a reason to pick another value in the open interval
   `(BACKGROUND_WARP_DEPTH, 0)`), documented as "lowest foreground gameplay
   layer: below every ship/enemy/bullet/pickup, above the background".
2. In the `Asteroid` constructor, call `this.setDepth(ASTEROID_DEPTH)` once
   (after `super(...)` / `addSharedGraphics()`), so the container renders below
   every default-depth (`0`) gameplay object.
3. Add a focused unit test (in `src/entities/Asteroid.test.ts` or a dedicated
   depth test) that pins the depth on a fresh asteroid and on a split child, and
   asserts the ordering against the gameplay baseline and background constants.
4. Add/extend a gym-parity assertion so the depth cannot drift between the game
   and an asteroid-bearing gym; record the layer in the parity docs.
5. Update the relevant docs/comments to describe the new lowest-foreground
   layer.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/constants.ts` — Add the exported `ASTEROID_DEPTH` constant alongside
  the existing depth constants (with a doc comment describing the layer).
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — Apply `this.setDepth(ASTEROID_DEPTH)` once in the
  constructor; note the layer in the module/class doc comment.
- `src/entities/Asteroid.test.ts` — New assertions: fresh asteroid depth, split
  child depth, strict ordering vs gameplay baseline (`0`) and background
  layers, intra-entity layer order unchanged.
- `src/scenes/core/asteroidHazard.ts` — Verify the shared spawn seam carries the
  depth (likely no change; the entity constructor owns it) and cover it in the
  test.
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — E6 asteroid section: record that
  asteroids render at the lowest foreground depth (layer note).
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` — Record the shared render-depth invariant where gym↔game
  parity is described (if a per-gym row is the right home).

## Related work

- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F** — Asteroids as an enemy (origin of the `Asteroid`
  entity, tiers, splitting, no-fire guarantee).
- **AH-0MW5088LA007XYQM** — Shared asteroid silhouette palette and single atlas
  (asteroid *rendering* work; the atlas/batching layer that this depth change
  must not disturb).
- **AH-0MW508UAQ002IC5N** — Asteroid rendering parity guard and docs row
  (precedent for an asteroid render-parity guard + docs update).
- **AH-0MVSEB7SA004B26C** — Shared background layer in combat core (the
  background depth layers the asteroid must stay above).
- **AH-0MUCST3BS0007CPT** — Mineral collectable entity and constants (precedent
  for an entity-owned depth constant, `MINERAL_DEPTH = 2`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

- `README.md` — matched: asteroids, away, lowest, make, value
- `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` — matched: asteroids, away, furthest, make, value
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: asteroids, away, lowest, make, value

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption (layer scope).** "Lowest (furthest away) z value" means the
  lowest **foreground** layer: below the player, other enemies, bullets,
  minerals and power-ups, but above the background/dim/warp layers. Rendering
  below the backdrop would make asteroids invisible, which is not the intent.
- **Assumption (value).** `-1` is used as the depth because it is the only
  simple integer strictly between the background warp layer (`-900`) and the
  gameplay baseline (`0`); if another foreground layer is later introduced
  between them, this constant is the single place to re-tune.
- **Risk (occlusion of collision feedback).** Placing rocks behind ships means
  an impact/explosion at the exact overlap point can be briefly occluded by the
  ship in front. Explosion particles/impacts are drawn at higher depths
  (`explosionGraphics` depth `2` within the container, plus shared impact VFX at
  positive depths), so feedback still lands above the ship in practice; verify
  during implementation.
- **Risk (parity drift).** If the depth were applied per-scene instead of on the
  shared entity, the game and a gym could diverge. Mitigation: apply it once on
  the entity and pin it with a parity test.
- **Scope-creep risk.** A full y-sorted pseudo-3D layering system for all
  gameplay entities is **out of scope**; this item only gives asteroids a fixed
  lowest foreground layer. Any broader depth-sorting work should be raised as a
  separate work item rather than folded in here.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q: What does "lowest (furthest away) z value" mean in this codebase
  — which layer should asteroids sit below?**
  — **Answer (assumption, recorded for producer confirmation):** The lowest
  **foreground** gameplay layer — below the player, all other enemies, bullets,
  minerals and power-ups, but above the background photo/dim/warp layers. The
  parenthetical "(furthest away)" is read as "most distant foreground object",
  not "behind the backdrop". Research: Phaser `depth` is the z-index
  (`node_modules/phaser/types/phaser.d.ts`); `src/core/constants.ts` defines
  background depths `-1000/-950/-900`, gameplay baseline `0`, minerals/bullets
  at positive depths, HUD `1000`; no existing asteroid render-order convention
  is documented in the GDD or `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md`.
  Source: repo inspection during intake.
- **Q: Should asteroids also render behind other enemies only, but above the
  player?**
  — **Answer (assumption):** No. "Lowest" is taken literally — asteroids are the
  most distant foreground object, so they render behind the player too. Source:
  intake reasoning; flagged here so the producer can correct it.
data.title: Make asteroids the lowest (furthest away) z value

## Problem

`node_modules/.vite` accumulates orphaned `deps_temp_<hash>` directories whenever a Vite dep optimisation is interrupted or collides — at intake there were 98 (141 MB), now **95 dirs / 158 MB total in `node_modules/.vite`**. They are pure cache debris: each is a partially written pre-bundle. The epic's AC3 timing work is unaffected functionally, but the debris wastes disk, slows directory scans, and is evidence that dep optimisation is re-running/colliding (which is one source of the transform/import variance measured in AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG).

## Why this was not fixed inline

`node_modules` is **shared by every worktree on this host via symlink**; deleting the cache while another agent's suite is mid-run can corrupt that run. The producer rule 'never destroy another agent's work' applies, so the cleanup needs a safe, quiescent mechanism rather than an opportunistic `rm -rf`.

## Expected change

A small, documented, safe cleanup path — e.g. `scripts/clean-vite-cache.mjs` that:
- refuses to run when any `vitest`/`vite` process is alive (or requires `--force`),
- removes only `deps_temp_*` (never the valid `deps/` bundle or `deps_ssr`),
- reports bytes reclaimed, and
- is documented in `docs/dev/test-suite-timing.md` (cache-hygiene section) and optionally wired into `scripts/hygiene_check.sh`.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1:** A read-only `--dry-run` (default) reports the orphaned `deps_temp_*` count and bytes; `--apply` removes only those dirs and prints the reclaimed bytes.
- **AC2:** The script refuses to delete while a `vitest`/`vite` process is running unless `--force` is passed, and is covered by tests (dry-run classification, refusal path) that do not require a real cache.
- **AC3:** Documentation states why the cache is shared across worktrees and why the quiescence guard exists.
- **AC4:** After `--apply` on an idle host, `npx vitest run --project unit` still passes (cache regenerates cleanly).

## References

- AH-0MVF6Y29M005TEOG — measured the transform/import cost and rejected the optimizer/isolate/pool variants; notes the collision evidence.
- `scripts/hygiene_check.sh` — the existing periodic hygiene report this could extend.
data.title: Vite dep-cache hygiene: 95 orphaned deps_temp_* dirs (158 MB) in node_modules/.vite

# Align AI_Hell's test framework with the Tableau-Card-Engine game repos

AI_Hell runs a bespoke Vitest setup: `vitest.config.ts` + `vitest.projects.ts` with a
static classifier (`classifyTestFiles` / `isIntegrationTest` in `vitest.projects.ts`)
splitting test files into `unit` / `integration` projects, and test roots `src/`,
`scripts/`, `vite/` — there is **no top-level `tests/` directory**. Every sibling TCE
game repo (and the scaffold template `core/scripts/game-repo-scaffold.ts`) uses the
standard layout: a `unit` project in `vite.config.ts` with
`include: ['tests/**/*.test.ts']` and no per-file classifier.

**Goal:** bring AI_Hell's test layout and project selection into line with the sibling
repos so cross-repo conventions, agent/audit tooling expectations (top-level `tests/`
tree), and the test skill's type profiles apply uniformly.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **No test lost or doubled.** After migration, AI_Hell's full suite runs the
   identical set of `*.test.ts` files currently selected by
   `vitest.projects.ts::allTestFiles` (src/, scripts/, vite/) — same count and same
   per-file project membership; verified by a before/after selection diff.
2. **Standard layout adopted.** Tests live under a top-level `tests/` tree laid out to
   match sibling repos (e.g. `tests/deploy/` for infra guards, `tests/<area>/`),
   selected via the standard include globs in `vitest.config.ts` (or the config file's
   `test.projects`), with `tsconfig.json` including `tests/**/*.ts`.
3. **Isolation preserved.** Phaser/DOM-booting tests retain their separation from the
   fast node `unit` project (the deliberate unit/integration split — parent
   AH-0MVF3BESP005ZDAV, blocked child AH-0MVF6XV87001NSEJ). Alignment must NOT flatten
   Phaser-heavy tests into the node unit project or regress suite runtime. The
   `src/test/projectMembership.test.ts` guard is updated to assert the new layout and
   still passes.
4. **Tooling keeps working.** The test skill's per-type profiles
   (`.pi/skills_extensions/test/extension.json`, `.pi/test-config.json`) remain
   functional — update only if project names/commands change, and verify each type
   (`unit`, `coverage`, `e2e`) runs.
5. **Documentation updated.** Comments in the vitest config(s), AGENTS.md and any
   dev notes reflect the new layout. CHANGELOG.md excluded (ship skill).
6. **Full suite passes** with the changes.

## Constraints

- Refactor only — no change to app behaviour.
- Preserve the deterministic membership guard pattern (`vitest.projects.ts` is
  deliberately the single source of truth for selection; keep an equivalent guard).
- This item may also relocate `vite/viteWatchIgnore.test.ts` (added by the watch-ignore
  port, MS-0MVBEQ6MC004WRI0) into `tests/deploy/` for full parity — sequence after or
  alongside that port.
